You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: In the support chat I ask "Where is order A-1003?" and the assistant answers politely but without any details, saying it cannot get the information right now. There is no error. It happens for every order and every refund request, although the order desk on its own still answers correctly.
Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. Then write `answer.json` in the project root: { "file": "<path of the file that had the bug>", "snippet": "<the exact broken text you replaced, copied verbatim, one line is enough>", "cause": "<one sentence>", "evidence": "<what shows this is the cause>" }. Don't change `package.json` or add dependencies.

I'm trying to figure out which flow is actually responsible—the plain support chat with no tools, or the triage agent that delegates to orderAgent—since the bug report of a vague "can't get information right now" response could stem from either path depending on how the failure is surfaced.

My current suspicion is the `agents` middleware config on triage, maybe something like `maxDelegations: 0` blocking delegation entirely, which would produce exactly this generic refusal even though the order desk works fine standalone. I want to check the middleware's delegation semantics and the orders data itself to rule out a missing order ID before settling on this theory.
The chat flow has no tools, and the triage agent delegates through `agents({ ... maxDelegations: 0 })`. That `0` looks suspicious, so I'll check what the middleware does with it.

text:
With maxDelegations at 0, every delegation attempt would hit the limit and return a blocked message, which matches the bug where the triage model can't fetch info for both order and refund flows while the order desk alone still works. I need to check whether the "support chat" actually refers to the triage flow or the separate chat flow, since the chat flow doesn't use tools and wouldn't produce that "cannot get info" message.

I'm leaning toward the triage agent being the actual "support chat" since its job is routing customer messages, while the standalone chat flow lacks an order lookup tool entirely and would give a permanent "can't look up orders" answer rather than the transient "right now" failure described in the bug. Since the bug notes that the order desk still answers correctly on its own, and the chat flow never even calls the order desk, that points the issue toward the triage path instead.

The real culprit looks like `maxDelegations: 0` in the triage config, which would immediately trigger "Delegation limit reached" whenever it tries to delegate to the order desk — explaining why it can't get the information right now despite the order desk working fine independently. The cleanest fix is removing that line entirely so delegation is unbounded, since triage already has `maxTurns: 5` as a natural limit anyway.

I'll settle on removing `maxDelegations: 0,` entirely rather than guessing a replacement number, since omitting it defaults to unlimited and maxTurns: 5 already bounds runaway loops.

Before making the edit, I want to double-check the surrounding flow — confirming the delegation tool response actually gets returned to the model, and scanning the triage/chat path for any other hidden issue like toolChoice settings. I also want to verify orders.json contains A-1003 as supporting evidence, and confirm orderAgent works fine on its own since it has no maxDelegations setting.
The `maxDelegations: 0` guard in `triage` makes every delegation return "Delegation limit reached (0)". Next I'll confirm the rest of the delegation path and check the order data for A-1003.

text:
The root cause was in the triage agent's config in `src/agents.ts`: it set `maxDelegations: 0`, so the middleware rejected every hand-off to the order desk or refund desk. I removed that option. Live runs now return A-1003's status, ETA and tracking code, and forward a refund request for approval.

`answer.json` is written at the project root. `package.json` is unchanged and no dependencies were added.

If "support chat" in your report means the `chat` flow in `src/flows.ts` rather than the triage agent, that is a different gap. That flow has no `lookupOrder` tool, so it cannot look up orders at all. I left it alone because the bug report points at the order desk working on its own.
